title: Enriched isomorphism from a tensor-preserving left adjoint
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] with tensor bifunctors and bifunctors $H_{\mathcal C},H_{\mathcal D}$ contravariant in the first variable. Assume bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes X,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(X,Y))$ natural in all variables; evaluation is the inverse image of the identity. Let $F\dashv G$ have unit $u$, counit $e$ and normalized adjunct $h^\sharp=e_NFh$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Let $\mu_{X,Y}:FX\otimes FY\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X\otimes Y)$ be natural. For $P\in\mathcal C$, $N\in\mathcal D$, put $V=H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)$ and $J=H_{\mathcal D}(FP,N)$. Let $b:FV\to J$ be the closed transpose of $e_NF(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\mu_{V,P}$. Then its adjunct $$\delta_{P,N}=G(b)u_V:H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)\xrightarrow{\sim}G H_{\mathcal D}(FP,N)$$ is an isomorphism, natural in both inputs. No tensor associator, unit coherence, full faithfulness or dualizability hypothesis is needed.

proof.text:
Write $\Theta^{\mathcal C}$ and $\Theta^{\mathcal D}$ for the assumed closed bijections, and $\Psi_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,GY)$ for the given adjunction bijection. In either category, naturality in $T$ gives
$$\Theta\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}\circ(t\otimes1_X)\bigr)=\Theta(\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y})\circ t=t,$$
for $t:T\to H(X,Y)$. Bijectivity therefore gives the explicit uncurrying formula $\Theta^{-1}(t)=\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}\circ(t\otimes1_X)$. Only the definition of evaluation, the assumed naturality, and the category identity laws of [def-nagata-category] enter.

proof.text:
Fix $P,N$ and use the objects $V,J$ in the statement. For every object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, compose the following bijections:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,V)&\xrightarrow{(\Theta^{\mathcal C})^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T\otimes P,GN)\xrightarrow{\Psi^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(T\otimes P),N)\\
&\xrightarrow{(-)\circ\mu_{T,P}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FT\otimes FP,N)\xrightarrow{\Theta^{\mathcal D}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FT,J)\xrightarrow{\Psi}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,GJ).
\end{aligned}$$
Call this bijection $\Phi_T$. The middle map is bijective by precomposition with $\mu_{T,P}^{-1}$ as its inverse. The two uses of $\Psi$ and their directions are exactly the natural bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Its formula $\Psi^{-1}(h)=e_N\circ Fh$, together with step 1, gives
$$\Phi_T(t)=\Psi_{T,J}\!\left(\Theta^{\mathcal D}\!\left(e_N\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ F(t\otimes1_P)\circ\mu_{T,P}\right)\right).$$

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), natural Hom bijections and the adjunction-map formulas immediately following the definition; agent-written closed-bifunctor calculation for the mapping-complex comparisons in prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, proof paragraph 2.

proof.text:
Put $r=e_N\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ\mu_{V,P}:FV\otimes FP\to N$, so the specified $b$ is $\Theta^{\mathcal D}(r)$. Naturality of $\mu$ at $(t,1_P)$ gives
$$F(t\otimes1_P)\circ\mu_{T,P}=\mu_{V,P}\circ(Ft\otimes1_{FP}).$$
Consequently the inner transpose in step 2 is
$$\Theta^{\mathcal D}\bigl(r\circ(Ft\otimes1_{FP})\bigr)=\Theta^{\mathcal D}(r)\circ Ft=b\circ Ft$$
by the assumed naturality in the first (test-object) variable. Finally, the source naturality and unit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] give
$$\Phi_T(t)=\Psi_{T,J}(b\circ Ft)=\Psi_{V,J}(b)\circ t=G(b)\circ u_V\circ t=\delta_{P,N}\circ t.$$
Thus postcomposition with the specified $\delta$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the objects, is bijective for every $T$.

proof.text:
Write $W=GJ$ and $\delta=\delta_{P,N}:V\to W$. Surjectivity of $\Phi_W$ gives $s:W\to V$ with $\delta\circ s=1_W$. Hence
$$\delta\circ(s\circ\delta)=(\delta\circ s)\circ\delta=\delta=\delta\circ1_V.$$
Injectivity of $\Phi_V$, identified in step 3 with postcomposition by $\delta$, gives $s\circ\delta=1_V$. Therefore $s$ is a two-sided inverse and $\delta$ is an isomorphism. The displayed simplifications use only the identity and associativity laws of [def-nagata-category]. This supplies the elementary Hom-test argument explicitly; no representability or size theorem is being invoked.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-closed-adjunction-naturality] to precisely the two tensor bifunctors, the given three-variable natural closed bijections, the natural isomorphisms $\mu$, and the adjunction $F\dashv G$ of this statement. Its $b$ is the closed transpose of $e_N\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ\mu_{V,P}$ and its $\delta$ is $G(b)\circ u_V$, so both are the actual maps used here. The cited statement gives, for arbitrary $a:P'\to P$ and $v:N\to N'$,
$$\delta_{P',N'}\circ H_{\mathcal C}(a,Gv)=G H_{\mathcal D}(Fa,v)\circ\delta_{P,N}.$$
These are the two-variable naturality squares. Step 4 makes every component invertible, so these maps form the required natural isomorphism. The naturality lemma assumes only the same bifunctors and natural bijections, with no associator, unit coherence, full faithfulness or dualizability condition.
